author_reading.rationale: Two unrelated flags are synchronized separately and reconverge in the output word with no shared capture protocol.

rationale: Each scalar has two destination stages. Assignment to two-bit registers zero-extends each input; the ten-bit output concatenation loses only leading zeros. The meaningful bits remain independent observations. Concatenation alone proves neither a correlation requirement nor independence. Without a consumer contract this cannot be called an unsafe coherent transfer or a whole-IP good control. Physical synchronizer implementation and asynchronous reset release/recovery remain external obligations; neither SDC nor sampled digital simulation closes them.

labels.rationale: a and b each pass through a separate two-stage clk_b chain, with no logical reconvergence or specified correlation requirement. The two-bit declarations zero-extend each scalar; output truncation removes leading zeros only. This is structurally suitable for independent level signals. Correlated use, event delivery, physical synchronization and reset recovery would require additional contracts; none is demonstrated as a defect here.

Each scalar input has two destination stages. Zero extension into two-bit registers and output truncation leave the two scalar values visible. Mere concatenation does not prove they require correlation: independent status controls can be safe, correlated controls can produce an invalid combination. The missing independence/coherence contract prevents deciding between them. Physical implementation and reset closure remain separate.
